issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's map cons_v_f is defined with conv D_F, and the density Lemma lem:edlem9 is stated for the conv-based map, but in the proof the auxiliary map is defined as cons_v_L(y, theta) = D_F(x, theta) + (singleton) without the convex hull. The definable selection (z(t), w(t)) therefore lies in D_F, not conv D_F, and the chain rule for F along (x(t), theta(t)) is established only for elements (0, u) in D_F(x, theta) + S. Elements (0, u) in conv D_F(x, theta) + S outside D_F(x, theta) + S, which is what the theorem's cons_v_f and lem:edlem9's density argument produce, are never shown to satisfy the chain rule; as written, the proof establishes the chain rule property for a strictly smaller set-valued map than the stated cons_v_f.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define cons_v_L in the proof with conv D_F (matching the theorem statement and lem:edlem9), take the selection (z(t), w(t)) from conv D_F(x(t), theta(t)), and justify the chain rule for F with this selection by the standard convexification property of conservative fields (the convex hull of a conservative field is again conservative for F, since the chain rule holds for all elements of D_F simultaneously almost everywhere and hence for convex combinations). No other change is needed and the statement of theo:main is unchanged.

issues.title: Proof of Theorem theo:main defines cons_v_L without the convex hull, so the chain rule is established only for a strictly smaller map than the stated cons_v_f
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line correction (insert the convex hull in the proof's definition of cons_v_L) plus a standard fact from the conservative-calculus literature that the paper already relies on elsewhere; no substantive claim, rate, or advertised scope is lost and the theorem's statement stands.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any \(k \in \N\), consider \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k)\) such that \(r_k > 0\), \(r_k \xrightarrow[k \to \infny]{} 0\), and \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k) \cap \Bcal(z_{s},r_{s}) = \varnothing\) for \(s \neq k\).
Such a choice is possible, because for each $k$, $z_k$ is at positive distance of \(z_i\) for each $i \neq k$ and at positive distance of \(C\) the set of accumulation points.
Then we have, for any \(k \in \N\), \(\nabla \bar{g}(\bar{z}_k) = \nabla \bar{f}(\bar{z_k}) + v\).
Thanks to Lemma \myref{lem:subseqtocantor}, there exists a sequence \((z_k)_{k\in\N} \subset \R^2 \setminus C\) such that its set of accumulation points is \(C\).

issues.failure_explanation: The bumps phi(||z-z_k||/r_k) r_k have gradients of magnitude 1 at z_k - (r_k/2)v (since phi'(1/2) = -1) and their supports accumulate at every point of C, because (z_k) has C as its exact accumulation set. The stated conditions on the radii (r_k > 0, r_k -> 0, pairwise disjoint balls) do not relate r_k to dist(z_k, C); not even r_k <= dist(z_k, C), which is needed for gbar = 0 on C, is imposed. For admissible choices with r_k comparable to dist(z_k, C) the asserted differentiability fails: already for C = {0}, z_k = 2^{-k}, r_k = 2^{-k-1}, at z = 0 the difference quotient along h = z_k + r_k/2 equals phi(1/2) r_k/||h|| + o(1) = (9/32)(2/5) + o(1) > 0, while along h = -2^{-k} it tends to 0 (since grad fbar(0) = 0); hence the limit does not exist and gbar is not differentiable at 0. In general, whenever z_k -> z in C with ||z_k - z|| comparable to r_k, the quotient along h = (z_k - z) + (r_k/2)v stays bounded away from 0 while bump-avoiding directions give 0. The claim is repaired by imposing r_k = o(dist(z_k, C)) (e.g. r_k <= dist(z_k, C)^2): then ||h|| >= dist(z_k, C) - r_k >> r_k whenever z + h lies in B(z_k, r_k), so the bump contribution is o(||h||), gbar is differentiable on C with vanishing gradient, and the inclusion of the unit ball in the Clarke subdifferential (which follows from grad gbar(z_k - (r_k/2)v) = grad fbar(z_k - (r_k/2)v) + v independently of r_k) and all other asserted properties are preserved.

failure_location.quote:
Define \(\bar{g}\colon \Rell \to \R\) as 
\[
z \mapsto \bar{f}(\vz) + \sum_{k \in \N} \varphi\left(\frac{\norm{\vz - \vz_k}}{r_k}\right)r_k. 
\]
Then, \(\bar{g}(z)= 0\) for every \(z \in C\), and \(\bar{g}(z) > 0\) for every \(z \in \Rell \setminus C\). Moreover  \(\bar{g}\) is differentiable and locally Lipschitz on \(\Rell\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the choice of radii to r_k = o(dist(z_k, C)) (for instance r_k <= min(dist(z_k, C)^2, 1/k)) while keeping the balls pairwise disjoint and disjoint from C; then the same function is differentiable on C with vanishing gradient, vanishes exactly on C, and all other asserted properties, including the Clarke-subdifferential inclusion and path differentiability, are unaffected, so the claim and the dependent counterexample go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The existence claim of lem:fnctcounterex (a differentiable, locally Lipschitz, path-differentiable function vanishing exactly on C with the unit ball contained in its Clarke subdifferential on C) is unproved as written, and the counterexample Claim theo:counterex, which takes its objective F from lem:fnctcounterex, loses its support.
issues.title: In lem:fnctcounterex the bump construction is not differentiable on C as asserted: the stated conditions on the radii permit non-differentiable outcomes
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local strengthening of the hypothesis on the radii together with a routine difference-quotient estimate; it adds no new lemma or construction, and the claim, all its stated properties, and the dependent counterexample survive intact.
